questions: How must the recovered post-blend split-inheritance correction be integrated across sequence-player, single-node, and direct playback paths, and which rendered retail invariant validates it?

What do the chain-rebase branch's shorts at remap record +0x04 and +0x06 select, and which corpus reaches that branch at all? The branch structure, the parent-chain walk against the included model's StudioBone.parent, and the position-transform byte are read; no shipped model in the captured corpus carries a record that enters it, and its second loop cannot terminate unless the two shorts are equal.
Which model/material decode defect causes the observed rainbow cloth independently of skeletal pose?

Which client receive/update path applies the server's networked activity and m_nSequence changes before SetupBones, and which sequence changes can originate only on the client? The server selector functions are located and tracked in gameplay_actions.json; this client-side specification now owns only the state handoff into pose evaluation.

How does the MDLHeader +396/+400 record table construct, update, constrain and render table-driven hair and body chains? The writer and four runtime parameters are located; record +8 remains unnamed and both recovered client constructors omit it.

field_probes.label: bone_cache_or_mask
field_probes.role: Enumerates users of the C_BaseAnimating field used by SetupBones and BuildTransformations while locating the returned bone-matrix buffer.

field_probes.label: secondary_chain_list
field_probes.role: Enumerates readers and writers of C_BaseAnimating's linked list of MDLHeader +396/+400 bone-chain owners.

field_probes.label: client_entity_ref_handle
field_probes.role: C_BaseEntity's own EHANDLE, whose low 13 bits are the client entity index. Enumerates every reader so the capture's direct field read is grounded in the population the two accessors serve.

findings.fact: The local quaternion and position channel decoders do not read bone Flags & 0x2.
findings.evidence: 0x10089b20 calls 0x100889f0 and 0x10088ba0 for each selected bone; neither decoder reads flags@bone+0x88.
findings.consequence: The flag is a post-decode hierarchy/application rule, not an alternate RLE encoding.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones dispatches the standard pose builder through vtable +0x208 and BuildTransformations through vtable +0x1ec.
findings.evidence: 0x10091c17-0x10091c5e; C_BaseAnimating slots 0x101e3f04=0x10091650 and 0x101e3ee8=0x1008fd00.
findings.consequence: The decoded pose, hierarchy construction, and entity/root composition are all on the live render-pose path.

findings.fact: BuildTransformations gives Flags & 0x2 bones split inheritance: rotation is root/entity rotation times local rotation, while translation is parent bone-to-world times local position.
findings.evidence: 0x1008ffa2-0x100901b5; flag test at 0x1008ffc5, custom branch at 0x1008fff3.
findings.consequence: A normal glTF node hierarchy and any fixed per-key quaternion multiplier are not faithful representations.

findings.fact: The BuildTransformations stack contract is positions, quaternions, root/entity 3x4 transform, then selected-bone bit list.
findings.evidence: SetupBones pushes the four arguments at 0x10091c3d-0x10091c5e; BuildTransformations consumes them at stack +0x6f60 through +0x6f6c.
findings.consequence: The special-bone rotation frame is the same entity/root transform used for root bones.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones is __thiscall with five callee-cleaned dword stack arguments, and its first five prologue bytes are one complete instruction with no relative operand.
findings.evidence: All four exits at 0x10091a2d, 0x10091a50, 0x100920cc and 0x100921cc are RET 0x14; 0x100919c0 is b830270000 (MOV EAX,0x2730) ahead of the _chkstk call at 0x101d0f00, and no instruction in the function branches to 0x100919c0-0x100919c4.
findings.consequence: The callee independently confirms the five arguments engine.dll stages, and the target takes an inline detour on the same shared backend as build_transformations without prologue relocation risk.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones receives the IClientRenderable subobject as this and adjusts down four bytes to reach the C_BaseAnimating, so its this equals the entity value the draw stream stores.
findings.evidence: 0x100919d6 moves ECX into EDI and 0x100919ea computes LEA ESI,[EDI-0x4] before dispatching on ESI; one theatre capture records the SetupBones bracket entity equal to the DrawModel render-info entity on every draw that resolved a bracket.
findings.consequence: This is CAP1.3's +4 seen from the other end: the skeletal evaluators run on the C_BaseAnimating while the renderable interface, the draw field, and SetupBones all share the subobject address, so a pose build joins a draw at delta zero and an evaluation at delta four.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::InternalDrawModel is __thiscall with two callee-cleaned dword stack arguments, and its first five prologue bytes are three complete instructions with no relative operand.
findings.evidence: All five exits at 0x10092983, 0x100929b4, 0x100929cc, 0x100932e9 and 0x1009335f are RET 0x8; 0x10092970 is 83ec7c5356 (SUB ESP,0x7c; PUSH EBX; PUSH ESI), and no instruction in the function branches to 0x10092970-0x10092974.
findings.consequence: The outer draw frame takes an inline detour on the same shared backend as resolve_virtual_model_pose, so a pose build and the StudioRender draw it feeds can be bracketed under one enclosing generation.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::InternalDrawModel submits the client renderable through VEngineModel006 slot +0x8.
findings.evidence: client.dll 0x10092f18-0x10092f51; VEngineModel006 acquisition at 0x100cb5e7-0x100cb5f3.
findings.consequence: The downstream SetupBones callback and palette application continue in engine.dll and StudioRender.dll, tracked by the companion specifications.

findings.fact: Transition history converts a saved pose with delta = inverse(currentRenderTransform) * savedEntityTransform before blending.
findings.evidence: client.dll 0x10091487-0x1009159c; AngleMatrix 0x101094b0, inverse 0x10108450, concat 0x10108a50, and raw stack arguments.
findings.consequence: Root and Flags-0x2 rotations are moved from the saved entity frame into the current render frame; root translation is moved too.

findings.fact: The outer included-model remap optionally transforms position by a per-record 3x4 matrix but always copies quaternion verbatim.
findings.evidence: client.dll 0x100969fb-0x10096ae8; 0x3c-byte mapping records and TransformPoint 0x10107f80.
findings.consequence: A faithful virtual-model resolver must retain authored position-frame mappings without inventing a rotation retarget at this layer.

findings.fact: A client entity class writes one vtable per subobject, and the second subobject sits at this+0x4.
findings.evidence: 0x10002d8b through 0x10002dab store 0x101e3cfc at +0x0, 0x101e3ca4 at +0x4, 0x101e3c6c at +0x8, 0x101e3c30 at +0xc and 0x101e3c1c at +0x10; C_BaseEntity::C_BaseEntity at 0x1008f3c0 writes the same five displacements with its own vtables at 0x1022d6d4, 0x1022d67c, 0x1022d644, 0x1022d608 and 0x1022d5f4, and C_BaseEntity::~C_BaseEntity restores exactly those five.
findings.consequence: CAP1.3's +4 is a declared multiple-inheritance layout rather than a heap coincidence: the interface subobject the draw stream and SetupBones both name is the second base, four bytes into the object, and the constructors say so independently of any capture. One theatre capture measures the same +4 between the entity and renderable addresses the actor census records.

findings.fact: A vtable carrying BuildTransformations at +0x1ec belongs to one concrete class rather than to every skeletal entity, so it does not identify a shared construction path.
findings.evidence: 0x101e3cfc carries slot +0x1ec = 0x1008fd00 and slot +0x208 = 0x10091650, the two dispatch targets SetupBones pins, yet exactly one instruction references it as data (0x10002d8b) and its writer 0x10002d80 has exactly one caller (0x10002c40). A hook installed on 0x10002d80 for a 90-second theatre capture recorded zero constructions while four skeletal actors were posed.
findings.consequence: Each derived class carries its own vtable with the same inherited slots, so a construction target must be the shared base C_BaseEntity::C_BaseEntity rather than any class whose vtable happens to hold the pose slots.

findings.fact: C_BaseEntity::C_BaseEntity is 0x1008f3c0 and C_BaseEntity::~C_BaseEntity is 0x1008f5c0; both are __thiscall with no stack arguments and both are the shared base of the client entity hierarchy.
findings.evidence: The constructor is 53 55 56 57 8b f1 (PUSH EBX; PUSH EBP; PUSH ESI; PUSH EDI; MOV ESI,ECX) with 12 callers; the destructor is 53 56 57 8b f9 (PUSH EBX; PUSH ESI; PUSH EDI; MOV EDI,ECX) with 15 callers and one exit at 0x1008f6e5 that restores this into ECX and JMPs to 0x1009ddc0 rather than returning. Each prologue is complete instructions with no relative operand, nothing branches into either, and the two are the only references to the vtable 0x1022d6d4.
findings.consequence: Every client entity construction and destruction passes through this pair, so a lifetime record covers the whole hierarchy; restricting it to the skeletal actors CAP2.3 names is an offline join against the actor census rather than a live filter.

findings.fact: Every Flags & 0x2 bone in the patch-first character corpus uses the conventional hierarchy-FK inverse bind, not a split-inheritance inverse bind.
findings.evidence: pipeline/src/elysium_pipeline/validation/validate_skeletal_pipeline.py independently evaluates all 373 flagged bones across 433 character skeletons; worst boneToWorld * poseToBone identity error is 7.36e-6.
findings.consequence: Split inheritance belongs only to live pose construction; skin binding and generated inverse binds remain conventional.

findings.fact: The pose chain below resolve_virtual_model_pose shares one seven-dword __cdecl contract: (studiohdr, positions, quaternions, sequence, cycle, poseParameters, boneMask).
findings.evidence: 0x100968a0 is __thiscall ending RET 0x18 and forwards its six stack arguments plus the studiohdr it obtains from 0x1008f900(-1) to 0x10089c40 at 0x1009693a, cleaning with ADD ESP,0x1c. 0x10089c40 reaches its arguments at frame+0x27c8..0x27e0 after MOV EAX,0x27c4 / _chkstk and ends in a bare RET, and stages the same seven for 0x10089740 at 0x1008a046 with ADD ESP,0x1c.
findings.consequence: A capture hook at either frame reads the owner studiohdr as argument zero rather than inferring it, and the two frames take the same argument decoder.

findings.fact: decode_selected_bones is __cdecl (studiohdr, positions, quaternions, StudioAnimDesc, cycle, boneMask); its fourth argument is the animation descriptor of one blend cell.
findings.evidence: 0x10089b20 reads its arguments at frame+0x04..0x18 after SUB ESP,0x8 and four pushes, and ends in a bare RET; the single-cell call site 0x1008993d builds the fourth argument as studiohdr + LocalAnimIndex@268 + grid cell * 72 and cleans with ADD ESP,0x18. The callee reads numframes at +0xc and animindex at +0x30 of that pointer.
findings.consequence: Owner-local animation identity is witnessed per fired cell as a pointer into the owner image, so CAP2.5's file offset is that pointer minus the studiohdr and the index is (pointer - hdr - LocalAnimIndex) / 72.

findings.fact: Frame selection is floor((numframes - 1) * cycle), and the remainder is the interpolation fraction passed to both channel decoders.
findings.evidence: 0x10089b41-0x10089b5e loads numframes@+0xc of the animation descriptor, decrements it, multiplies by the cycle argument, calls __ftol, and passes both the integer and the difference to 0x100889f0 and 0x10088ba0.
findings.consequence: Clip duration divides by frames - 1, not frames, which settles the sampling-law question the evidence document lists as open.

findings.fact: The per-bone animation records inside a StudioAnimDesc have a fixed 32-byte stride, and the selected-bone mask is a dword array beginning four bytes into the mask argument.
findings.evidence: 0x10089b20 walks NumBones@240 advancing the bone by 0xa0, positions by 0xc, quaternions by 0x10 and the animation record by 0x20 per bone, and gates each bone on mask[4 + (i >> 5) * 4] & (1 << (i & 31)).
findings.consequence: The animation block is indexable without decoding preceding bones, and the +4 the capture probe already copies is the array itself rather than a guessed displacement.

findings.fact: StudioSeqDesc carries the blend axes at groupsize[2]@572, paramindex[2]@580, paramstart[2]@588 and paramend[2]@596, and its 16x16 animation grid at 56 has a 32-byte row stride.
findings.evidence: 0x10089500 indexes all four arrays as base + axis * 4 off the descriptor; 0x10089740 branches on groupsize[1] then groupsize[0] at 0x100898fd to select one, two or four cells, reading grid[i1][i0] at descriptor+0x38+(i1*16+i0)*2 and grid[i1+1][i0] at descriptor+0x58+(i1*16+i0)*2. Across the installed character tree all 294 multi-blend sequences satisfy groupsize[0] * groupsize[1] == numblends@52, with distribution 9x1 235, 3x3 49, 2x1 6 and 5x1 4.
findings.consequence: The grid is a groupsize[0] by groupsize[1] blend space rather than a raw 16x16 array, and a decoder that reads only cell [0][0] silently drops every one of those 294 sequences.

findings.fact: A pose parameter descriptor is 20 bytes at LocalPoseParamIndex@388 with name@0, flags@4, start@8, end@12 and loop@16; a sequence axis normalizes its parameter into [0,1] over paramstart..paramend and clamps.
findings.evidence: 0x10089500 reads hdr+0x184 + index * 0x14 and uses +0x10 as a wrap modulus when non-zero, then normalizes (value - start@8) / (end@12 - start@8) and remaps through the descriptor's paramstart and paramend before clamping to 0..1 and deriving the cell index against groupsize. The installed corpus reads move_yaw and hit_yaw with flags 1, start -180, end 180 and loop 360, matching the -180/180 paramstart/paramend of every 9x1 sequence that selects them.
findings.consequence: Pose parameter range, wrapping, normalization and blend mapping are established, so a reproduced evaluator no longer has to guess whether values are normalized before lookup.

findings.fact: StudioSeqDesc carries an autolayer count at 660 and an autolayer index at 664, and each entry is a four-byte sequence index the dispatcher evaluates recursively.
findings.evidence: 0x1008a06b reads descriptor+0x294 as a loop bound and 0x1008a079 reads descriptor+0x298 as the array base, advancing four bytes per iteration and passing each dword as the sequence argument to a recursive 0x10089c40 call followed by 0x10088e10.
findings.consequence: A sequence contribution can fire further sequence contributions inside one pose build, so contribution multiplicity is a property of the data rather than of the caller.

findings.fact: The virtual sequence index space is the last include group's sequence base plus its count, and an index below NumLocalSeq@272 resolves against the model's own sequences.
findings.evidence: 0x100968e5-0x10096917 computes the bound from the last of NumIncludeModels@404 groups at IncludeModelIndex@408 with stride 0x74, reading base at group+0x08 and count at group+0x0c, and falls back to NumLocalSeq when the model has no include models; 0x10089c5b takes the local path on the same comparison.
findings.consequence: A captured sequence index is only meaningful beside the studiohdr it was resolved against, which is why owner identity travels on every contribution record.

findings.fact: A runtime include-model group is 116 bytes carrying the loaded model at +0x04, its sequence base at +0x08, its sequence count at +0x0c, a bone remap array at +0x10 with 56-byte records, and a 24-entry pose parameter remap at +0x44.
findings.evidence: 0x10089c84-0x10089d1b walks the groups at stride 0x74, calls vtable slot +0x4 on the object at group+0x04 to obtain the included studiohdr, remaps 0x18 pose parameter slots through the shorts at group+0x44, and then walks group+0x10 records advancing 0x38 per target bone.
findings.consequence: Owner resolution and the shared-animation remap are both reachable from the group entry, and the 24-slot pose parameter remap bounds the parameter span a contribution record must retain.

findings.fact: The three contribution frames take a five-byte inline detour without prologue relocation: 0x10089740 is a0c9024910, 0x10089c40 is b8c4270000, and 0x10089b20 is 83ec085355.
findings.evidence: Read from the pinned client.dll at file offsets for those RVAs; 0x10089740 is one MOV AL,moffs32 with an absolute operand, 0x10089c40 is one MOV EAX,imm32, and 0x10089b20 is SUB ESP,0x8 with two pushes. No branch inside any of the three targets a byte in its first five. The same extraction reproduces the already-installed setup_bones signature b830270000.
findings.consequence: All three take the shared inline backend on the same terms as the existing targets; 0x10089500 begins 83ec08538b5c241c and needs the instruction-aware relocation the backend already performs.

findings.fact: Both channel decoders share one six-dword __cdecl contract (studiohdr, int frame, float fraction, StudioBone, animation record, output), and neither reads the studiohdr it is given.
findings.evidence: 0x10089b20 pushes the six arguments in that order at 0x10089bae-0x10089bb4 and 0x10089bc5-0x10089bcf and cleans both calls with one ADD ESP,0x30; 0x100889f0 reads them at [ESP+0x14] and [ESP+0x18] before its first push and 0x10088ba0 at [ESP+0x10] through [ESP+0x18]; both end in a bare RET. Neither decompilation references parameter one after entry.
findings.consequence: A hook on either frame receives the animation record and the bone directly, so the per-bone span a cell dereferenced is witnessed rather than derived from animindex.

findings.fact: 0x10089b20 is the only caller of both channel decoders.
findings.evidence: DumpXrefs on 0x100889f0 reports one reference, an unconditional call at 0x10089bb4; on 0x10088ba0 one reference, an unconditional call at 0x10089bcf. Both sites are inside FUN_10089b20.
findings.consequence: Every channel decode is enclosed by one selected-bone loop, so a decoder frame cannot be reached except through the cell frame that owns it.

findings.fact: An animation record whose weight at +0 is zero ends the decode immediately: the output is zeroed and no channel offset, track byte or bone field is read.
findings.evidence: 0x100889f0 compares the float at the record base against 0x101e34f0 and 0x10088ba0 against the double at 0x10226fc8, and each writes three or four zeros and returns before touching anything else.
findings.consequence: Such a cell dereferences exactly the four weight bytes, so a consumed-span walk must stop there rather than attributing the whole record and its tracks to it.

findings.fact: The channel walk stops at the run holding the sampled frame rather than covering the track: it reads only the two header bytes of each run it skips, then that run's keys for the frame and the frame after it, reaching the following run's first key when the frame after it leaves the run.
findings.evidence: Both decoders load total at track+1, subtract it from the frame while total <= remaining and advance by valid*2+2, then index keys at run+2+frame*2 and run+2+(frame+1)*2, clamping to the last key at run+valid*2 and reading run+valid*2+4 when the run is exhausted. 0x10088ba0 additionally resets the frame to zero whenever a run declares total < valid.
findings.consequence: The bytes a cell dereferences inside a track are a small non-contiguous set determined by the frame, not the whole track, which is what CAP4.2 compares the exporter's whole-clip walk against.

findings.fact: The quaternion decoder reads quat at bone+44 for an unanimated channel and rotscale at bone+72 for an animated one; the position decoder reads pos at bone+32 as the base of every channel and posscale at bone+60 for an animated one.
findings.evidence: 0x100889f0 walks a cursor from bone+0x48 and reads cursor[-7] on the zero-offset branch; 0x10088ba0 walks a cursor from bone+0x3c, writes cursor[-7] into the output before testing the offset, and scales by the cursor otherwise. Neither reads flags at bone+136.
findings.consequence: The bind fields a cell dereferences are per channel and differ by decoder, so bone spans are attributed by channel rather than by whole StudioBone.

findings.fact: The two channel decoders take an inline detour over whole instructions with no relocated operand: 0x100889f0 is 8b4c241483ec20 over seven bytes and 0x10088ba0 is 8b4c2414d901 over six.
findings.evidence: Read from the pinned client.dll at the file offsets for those RVAs by the same section walk that reproduces the installed 83ec085355 and a0c9024910 signatures. 0x100889f0 is MOV ECX,[ESP+0x14] then SUB ESP,0x20; 0x10088ba0 is MOV ECX,[ESP+0x14] then FLD dword [ECX]. The lowest branch target inside either function is 0x10088a1f and 0x10088bc2 respectively, both past the stolen bytes.
findings.consequence: Both take the shared inline backend with no relocation declaration, the x87 opcode being one the backend's ModRM table already covers.

findings.fact: The client entity index is the low 13 bits of the entity's own EHANDLE at C_BaseEntity+0xe4.
findings.evidence: The constructor at 0x1008f3c0 installs five vtables, the primary at 0x1022d6d4 and subobject vtables at +4, +8, +0xc and +0x10; the +4 entry is the renderable CAP1.3 measured. Primary slot +0 is 0x1009f050, MOV [ECX+0xe4],EDX, and primary slot +4 is 0x1009f060, LEA EAX,[ECX+0xe4]; RET, so a setter and a getter independently name the same displacement. The 13-bit index and 19-bit serial split is shared with vampire.dll: client.dll carries 278 AND *,0x1fff against 269 SHR *,13 and vampire.dll 2227 against 2226, paired inside 48 bytes 191 and 1622 times.
findings.consequence: A client pose group can be joined to a server animation request on the index alone, bounded by the serial and by the witnessed lifetime of each address. This is the entity identity docs/vtmb/animation_and_movers.md records as missing from the render hook.

findings.fact: The include-model bone remap array is walked only on the include-group path. A sequence index below NumLocalSeq@272 jumps straight to the sequence evaluator and returns without reading any group, so a contribution whose owner is the model the dispatcher was entered with carries no remap at all.
findings.evidence: 0x10089c5b loads NumLocalSeq@0x110 and 0x10089c64 jumps to 0x1008a016 when the sequence argument is below it; that path reaches 0x1008a046's call to 0x10089740 and the autolayer loop, and never touches group+0x10. The remap loop at 0x10089d95-0x10089fe0 is reachable only from 0x10089cdd, which is entered after a group's range test and studiohdr accessor both succeed.
findings.consequence: Whether a contribution's position was remapped is a property of the route to its owner rather than of the owner or of the group's contents, so an offline evaluator must decide it per contribution from the include chain and not as a global rule.

findings.fact: A group owns a virtual sequence index only when all four of its tests pass: base@+0x08 <= index, index < base + count@+0x0c, the loaded model at +0x04 is non-null, and its vtable slot +0x04 returns a non-zero studiohdr. When no group owns the index the dispatcher sets the sequence to 0 and takes the local path.
findings.evidence: 0x10089c92-0x10089cb8 performs the four tests in that order and advances by 0x74 on any failure; 0x10089cd8 leaves the loop to 0x1008a01a, which zeroes the sequence argument before falling into 0x1008a016's local path. The recursion at 0x10089d5f is reached only after all four pass, and 0x10089d49 subtracts group+0x08 from the index to make it owner-local.
findings.consequence: An unloaded include model degrades to sequence 0 of the including model rather than faulting, and the group's sequence range is a runtime field, so no installed image can say which group a captured virtual index resolved through.

findings.fact: The 56-byte remap record is a short source bone@+0x00, a branch selector byte@+0x02, a position-transform byte@+0x03, two chain bone shorts at +0x04 and +0x06, and a row-major 3x4 matrix at +0x08. A negative source bone makes the dispatcher write the including model's own bind pose into the target instead of anything the included model decoded.
findings.evidence: 0x10089d95-0x10089da0 addresses the record at group + group[0x10] + index * 0x38 and reads the short at +0. 0x10089da6 branches on its sign to 0x10089da8, which reads StudioBone.pos@+0x20 and StudioBone.quat@+0x2c out of the including model's own BoneIndex@244 array at stride 0xa0. 0x10089de4 branches on the byte at +0x02 and 0x10089dee on the byte at +0x03; 0x10089e12 passes record+0x08 as the matrix argument of TransformPoint 0x10107f80. 0x10089ef7 and 0x10089efb read the shorts at +0x04 and +0x06.
findings.consequence: A bone the including model declares but the shared bank does not animate resolves to the target's own bind pose, which is the opposite of the donor-bind fallback the outer virtual-model remap produces, and the two must not be conflated.

findings.fact: The position-transform byte@+0x03 means the same thing in both branches: transform the resulting position through the record's own 3x4 matrix. The branches differ in the rotation. The copy branch copies the source quaternion verbatim; the chain-rebase branch decomposes the composed matrix, so it writes a rotation the source bone does not carry.
findings.evidence: In the copy branch 0x10089e24-0x10089e46 copies four dwords from the source quaternion at stride 0x10 regardless of the byte at +0x03. In the chain branch 0x10089f8c tests the same byte and either calls 0x10107e40 straight into the target pair or into a stack position that 0x10089fc1 then passes through 0x10107f80 with record+0x08. 0x10107e40 decomposes a 3x4 into a quaternion and a translation.
findings.consequence: The transform byte can be modelled once for both branches, and only the chain branch needs the parent-chain walk, so an evaluator that meets no chain-branch record needs the matrix multiply and nothing else.

findings.fact: The chain-rebase branch's second loop never advances its induction variable, so it terminates only when the shorts at record +0x04 and +0x06 are equal. A record carrying the two unequal would hang the engine, and no record in the captured corpus reaches the branch at all.
findings.evidence: 0x10089ef7 loads the short at +0x04 into EDI and 0x10089f24-0x10089f76 re-tests that same EDI against the short at +0x06 without writing it; the three calls in the body take EDI only as an input. Over the golden sp_theatre capture's 41 located remap arrays, 3,095 records split 2,352 copy-branch and 743 negative-source, and 0 carry a non-zero byte at +0x02.
findings.consequence: The open nested-remap question is not on the theatre path, so CAP5.8's numbers do not depend on closing it; the branch stays partial and needs a corpus that reaches it.

findings.fact: The bone mask handed to a resolved include model is rebuilt in that model's own bone index space, sized from its NumBones@240 and populated by mapping each set bit of the caller's mask through the group's remap array. It is not the caller's mask forwarded unchanged.
findings.evidence: 0x10089d1b-0x10089d2e calls 0x1008e370 as a __thiscall on a stack object with the caller's mask, the group's remap array base and the included studiohdr; 0x1008e370 reads NumBones@0xf0 from the studiohdr, zeroes ceil(bones/32) words, and for each set source bit sets the bit the remap short names when that short is non-negative. 0x10089d3e passes the rebuilt object as the recursion's seventh argument.
findings.consequence: CAP2.5's finding that the selected-bone set reaches the cell unchanged is a measured property of this corpus's remap arrays rather than a structural identity, so a corpus whose remap is not a bijection on the selected set would break it.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating owns one linked secondary-chain object per MDLHeader +396/+400 record at entity +0x724; a data/model change rebuilds the list and entity destruction frees it.
findings.evidence: 0x10096650 reads count@studiohdr+0x18c and offset@+0x190, allocates 0x50 bytes per 0x1c-byte record, calls 0x100ac0f0 and links the object at entity+0x724. The call at 0x10094bd5 rebuilds it; C_BaseEntity destruction calls 0x100966e0 at 0x1008f5e7.
findings.consequence: The table is a live per-entity dynamics system rather than metadata consumed by the offline model loader or by VPhysics.

findings.fact: Record +12 is gravity, +16 damping, +20 a spring exponent converted to pow(10,-value), and +24 a maximum angle converted from degrees to radians; record +8 is not passed by either recovered client constructor.
findings.evidence: 0x10096695-0x100966b2 and 0x1018adfe-0x1018ae1b both pass +24,+20,+16,+12,+4,+0 and never read +8. 0x100ac171-0x100ac1c5 converts and stores the values. Under bc_override, 0x100acac4-0x100acc64 maps bc_maxangle, bc_spring, bc_damp and bc_gravity onto the same four members.
findings.consequence: The four runtime fields are named by retail data flow rather than value-shape inference; +8 is verified client-unused and retains an unnamed compiler-side authoring value.

findings.fact: A -1 record terminal makes the constructor follow the ordered StudioBone.parent child chain from the first moving bone; a nonnegative terminal takes a separate explicit-chain branch, and the first moving bone must have a parent.
findings.evidence: 0x100ac12b-0x100ac16e emits the literal rootless-bone warning. 0x100ac1bc branches on -1; 0x100ac243-0x100ac279 appends children whose parent equals the current chain tail, while 0x100ac1cb-0x100ac241 walks the explicit-terminal form backward. All 600 installed records use -1.
findings.consequence: Automatic chain construction is confirmed; the explicit-terminal branch remains unexercised by shipped authored data.

findings.fact: The secondary-chain update is a stateful Verlet-like solve targeting 300 Hz, capped at ten catch-up steps, with a 0.001-second no-advance threshold and reset across gaps above 0.15 seconds.
findings.evidence: 0x100ac8a2-0x100ac8c9 compares against float 0.001; 0x100ac974-0x100ac988 compares the gap against double 0.15; 0x100acc64-0x100acc9c computes ceil(delta*300) and caps at 10. 0x100ad1c0 carries current/previous points with damping and gravity; 0x100ad2c0 applies the spring and max-angle constraint.
findings.consequence: A faithful port needs persistent chain state, discontinuity handling and substeps; a stateless angular clamp is not the retail algorithm.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::BuildTransformations runs every secondary-chain update after ordinary hierarchy composition and before returning the bone-to-world buffer to StudioRender.
findings.evidence: 0x100901f7-0x10090235 loads entity+0x724, walks the linked list and calls 0x100ac880 at 0x1009022c after the selected-bone composition loop ends at 0x100901f1.
findings.consequence: The previously bounded post-composition writer is located exactly, and its output reaches the normal StudioRender palette and CPU skinning path.

functions.label: dispatch_model_pose
functions.role: Resolves a virtual sequence index to its owning include model on the group's runtime sequence range, rebuilds the bone mask and the 24 pose parameters in that model's index space, recurses with the owner-local index, maps the result back through the group's 56-byte bone remap array, and then evaluates the descriptor's autolayers recursively. An index below NumLocalSeq takes the local path and no remap runs. The chain-rebase branch of the remap record is the one part still open, and no shipped model in the captured corpus reaches it.

functions.label: evaluate_sequence_pose
functions.role: Resolves both blend axes through 0x10089500, selects one, two or four cells of the sequence descriptor's 16x16 animation grid on the two group sizes, and calls the per-bone animation loop once per cell.

functions.label: resolve_blend_axis_weight
functions.role: Maps one pose parameter onto one blend axis of a sequence descriptor, wrapping and normalizing it against the parameter descriptor and the axis range, and returning the cell index and the fractional weight evaluate_sequence_pose blends with. Four callers: two per evaluation from 0x10089740 and two from 0x1008c060.

functions.label: decode_selected_bones
functions.role: Walks selected bones and decodes quaternion and position channels.

functions.label: decode_bone_quaternion
functions.role: Decodes four quaternion RLE channels, falls back to bind components, and interpolates frames.

functions.label: decode_bone_position
functions.role: Decodes three position RLE channels relative to bind position.

functions.label: resolve_virtual_model_pose
functions.role: Selects the base or included studio model and maps its pose into target arrays.

functions.label: transform_point_3x4
functions.role: Applies a 3x4 affine matrix to a position; used by transformed virtual-model mapping records.

functions.label: invert_rigid_3x4
functions.role: Inverts an orthonormal 3x4 entity transform for transition-history frame conversion.

functions.label: matrix_get_column
functions.role: Extracts a 3-vector matrix column; transition history uses column three to update a root position.

functions.label: angle_position_matrix
functions.role: Builds a 3x4 transform from Source angles and position for saved/current entity frames.

functions.label: maintain_sequence_transitions
functions.role: Maintains 0x4c-byte previous-sequence records, resolves their poses, moves root/Flags-0x2 orientation through saved/current entity frames, and blends them into the current pose.

functions.label: build_standard_pose
functions.role: Widely shared virtual pose builder: base sequence, transition history, autoplay sequences, virtual hook, then bone controllers.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_build_transformations
functions.role: C_BaseAnimating::BuildTransformations; builds bone-to-world matrices from local positions/quaternions and applies the Flags-0x2 split-inheritance rule.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_setupbones
functions.role: C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones entry point; manages cache/masks and dispatches pose construction plus model-space matrix construction through virtual slots.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_get_studio_hdr
functions.role: Resolves the entity's studiohdr_t from the model cache; called with -1 for the entity's own model. The capture probe calls it rather than hooking it, so the skeletal streams name the same header the draw stream reads.

functions.label: build_layered_pose
functions.role: Specialized pose builder: base sequence, transition history, weighted layers/overlays, virtual hook, then bone controllers.

functions.label: procedural_geometry_pose_consumer
functions.role: Large specialized consumer that samples poses while generating procedural geometry; it is not the base SetupBones hierarchy bridge.

functions.label: bone_cache_accessor
functions.role: Small reader of the C_BaseAnimating +0x6e8 field; inspect ownership and return semantics.

functions.label: bone_cache_consumer_a
functions.role: Consumes the +0x6e8 field after bone setup; candidate downstream matrix user.

functions.label: bone_cache_consumer_b
functions.role: Consumes the +0x6e8 field near SetupBones; candidate cache copy or render bridge.

functions.label: setupbones_direct_caller_a
functions.role: One of three direct client.dll callers of C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones; inspect for an override or downstream submission bridge.

functions.label: setupbones_direct_caller_b
functions.role: One of three direct client.dll callers of C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones; inspect for an override or downstream submission bridge.

functions.label: setupbones_direct_caller_c
functions.role: One of three direct client.dll callers of C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones; inspect for an override or downstream submission bridge.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_drawmodel
functions.role: C_BaseAnimating::DrawModel render entry; dispatches an internal drawing virtual after establishing render state.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_internal_drawmodel
functions.role: C_BaseAnimating main-vtable slot +0x1f4 reached from DrawModel; submits the renderable through VEngineModel006 slot +0x8.

functions.label: concrete_animating_construct
functions.role: Constructor of one concrete class derived from C_BaseAnimating; writes the vtable 0x101e3cfc whose slots the pose specification samples. It has one caller and a theatre capture hooked on it recorded no construction, so it is not the shared skeletal construction path.

functions.label: c_baseentity_construct
functions.role: C_BaseEntity::C_BaseEntity; writes the five C_BaseEntity subobject vtables at 0x1022d6d4 and has 12 callers, so every client entity's construction chain reaches it.

functions.label: c_baseentity_destruct
functions.role: C_BaseEntity::~C_BaseEntity; restores the same five subobject vtables at entry and tail-calls its base teardown, and has 15 callers, so every client entity destruction passes through it.

functions.label: c_baseentity_get_ref_ehandle
functions.role: C_BaseEntity::GetRefEHandle; primary vtable slot +4, returning this+0xe4. One of the two independent accessors that fix the client handle displacement.

functions.label: c_baseentity_set_ref_ehandle
functions.role: C_BaseEntity::SetRefEHandle; primary vtable slot +0, storing into this+0xe4. The second accessor, which agrees with the getter on the displacement.

functions.label: remap_bone_mask
functions.role: Rebuilds a selected-bone mask in a resolved include model's own bone index space, sized from its NumBones@240 and populated by mapping each set source bit through the group's 56-byte remap records.

functions.label: accumulate_layer_pose
functions.role: Accumulates one evaluated layer onto the running local pose. Decompiled from VtMB: bit 0x4 at 0x10088efc selects straight accumulation over the complementary-weight blend, and within it bit 0x10 selects FUN_10088d60 over FUN_10088d00; position accumulates as pos1 += pos2*s in both sub-branches. Valve's source-sdk-2013 SlerpBones() carries the same control flow under the names STUDIO_DELTA/STUDIO_POST - a shared-ancestor correspondence that supplies vocabulary only. VtMB forked Source before its public release and v2531 already diverges structurally, so the behaviour above rests on this binary, not on the SDK.

functions.label: combine_layer_quat_pre
functions.role: Bit-0x10-CLEAR additive combine, decompiled from VtMB: out = normalize(scale(layer,s) * base) - the scaled layer pre-multiplies. No VtMB sequence takes this branch; every _delta carries 0x14. Corresponds to Valve's QuaternionSM by shape.

functions.label: combine_layer_quat_post
functions.role: Bit-0x10-SET additive combine, decompiled from VtMB and taken by all 118 _delta sequences: out = normalize(base * scale(layer,s)) - the running pose stays on the left. This order is the one Unreal's AAT_LocalSpaceBase does not implement; every stock Unreal additive mode pre-multiplies. Corresponds to Valve's QuaternionMA by shape.

functions.label: quaternion_multiply
functions.role: Hamilton product out = p*q, preceded by an align of q into p's hemisphere. Verified component-by-component against the Hamilton identity from VtMB's own float math, independently of any SDK. Same operand convention as Unreal's VectorQuaternionMultiply.

functions.label: quaternion_scale
functions.role: Scales a quaternion's rotation by a scalar weight - the q^s the two additive combines apply before multiplying. Role read from its use sites in this binary.

functions.label: secondary_chain_rebuild
functions.role: Replaces the entity+0x724 linked list with one chain owner per 28-byte MDLHeader +396/+400 record and passes the consumed record fields to 0x100ac0f0.

functions.label: secondary_chain_rebuild_by_model_handle
functions.role: Builds the alternate entity+0x40 secondary-chain list from the same 28-byte records and passes the same six fields as 0x10096650, omitting record +8.

functions.label: secondary_chain_destroy
functions.role: Destroys every secondary-chain object linked at entity+0x724; called by rebuild and C_BaseEntity destruction.

functions.label: secondary_chain_enabled
functions.role: Tests a record index against studiohdr+0x18c and the entity+0x788 per-record mask; the result drives bc_fade direction.

functions.label: secondary_chain_construct
functions.role: Constructs an automatic or explicit bone chain, converts max angle and spring exponent, derives bind-segment frames, and allocates 100 bytes of state per moving bone.

functions.label: secondary_chain_update
functions.role: Updates fade and optional ground state, handles time discontinuities, applies bc_override, runs bounded integration/constraint substeps and writes corrected bone-to-world matrices.

functions.label: secondary_chain_integrate
functions.role: Advances current/previous point state with step-ratio-scaled damped velocity, gravity and an optional ground-height clamp.

functions.label: secondary_chain_constrain
functions.role: Reconstructs chain segment orientation against the posed bone matrices, applies spring and maximum-angle constraints, preserves segment relationships and recomposes corrected matrices.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_resolve_follow_parent
functions.role: Resolves the follow-attach parent for a mod_studio entity. Reads the follow handle at this+0x188, requires the resolved parent's model type to equal 3 (mod_studio), and returns the parent's model context at +0x404; returns 0 when the handle is stale, the parent carries no model, or the parent is not mod_studio. Its two diagnostics are "mod_studio: MOVETYPE_FOLLOW with no model." and "Attached %s (mod_studio) to %s (%d)". Called by C_BaseAnimating::BuildTransformations, C_BaseAnimating::DrawModel and C_ServerRagdollAttached::SetupBones.
